item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro dice que la Policía Federal de Brasil le pidió su pasaporte
item.description: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro dijo el lunes que la policía federal le había solicitado que entregara su pasaporte tras visitar a su padre, el expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, que se encuentra en prisión.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro dijo el lunes que la policía federal le había solicitado que entregara su pasaporte tras visitar a su padre, el expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, que se encuentra en prisión. El senador, que fue derrotado el domingo por el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la segunda vuelta, dijo que tenía intención de cumplir con la petición y negó que haya previsto huir del país tras las elecciones. Flávio Bolsonaro dijo, sin aportar pruebas, que la solicitud de la policía se basaba en un fallo del magistrado del Tribunal Supremo Alexandre de Moraes. El máximo tribunal de Brasil y la policía federal no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. "Me ordenaron allí mismo, en la calle, que entregara mis pasaportes, y además tengo prohibido salir del país", dijo Bolsonaro en un vídeo publicado en las redes sociales. El senador añadió que el fallo de Moraes se basaba en unas declaraciones de su hermano menor, Eduardo Bolsonaro, quien comentó en un podcast la semana pasada que Flávio debería abandonar el país si perdía la segunda vuelta electoral frente a Lula. Lula logró un histórico cuarto mandato en las elecciones del domingo, con un resultado sorprendente que desafió las encuestas. Bolsonaro se negó a aceptar la derrota y dijo que solicitaría la anulación del resultado.

item.title: Russian attack on Kyiv kills one, injures 10, hits educational institution, metro station
item.description: A Russian missile attack on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Monday killed at least one person and injured 10, including students at a dormitory, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Russian missile attack on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Monday killed at least one person and injured 10, including students at a dormitory, officials said. The late-evening attack hit an educational institution, residences, an underground station and medical facilities. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, writing on Telegram, said one person had been killed near a supermarket. Ukraine's state rescue services said a body was found by a heavily damaged apartment building. Klitschko put the number of injured at 10, many of them outside a student dormitory at the State Trade and Economics University on the east side of the Dnipro River. Nine people were being treated in hospital, with three in serious condition. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, also writing on Telegram, gave no precise figures for dead and injured. "For the moment, the number of people is not exactly known," Zelenskiy said. "But, unfortunately, there are casualties. There are injured. Rescue operations are continuing." He repeated his call to eliminate delays in securing air defence arms quickly to counter Russian air attacks. "It is precisely in such conditions, when the threat is constant, when strikes can happen at any moment and on cities and villages, that artificial delays in air defence for Ukraine are helping terror," he said. Earlier in the day, Zelenskiy said Ukraine [USN:L5N46C0Z6 TEXT:"had been waiting"] for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on critical missile supplies. "In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again," the president said on X. Unofficial Telegram channels posted pictures of damage to an underground station and a tram. Klitschko said explosions shattered windows at two medical facilities. He said two members of an emergency crew had been injured after rushing to the scene of one strike. Reuters witnesses said a series of explosions jolted the city. They said power had been cut in districts on the east side of the Dnipro River. Moscow has long denied that it targets civilians.

item.title: Leinster's Furlong cited over alleged genital grabbing
item.description: Veteran Ireland prop Leinster's Tadhg Furlong has been cited for allegedly grabbing the genitals of Munster's Gavin Coombes during their United Rugby Championship match at the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Veteran Ireland prop Leinster's Tadhg Furlong has been cited for allegedly grabbing the genitals of Munster's Gavin Coombes during their United Rugby Championship match at the weekend. Coombes alleged during the game on Saturday that his testicles had been grabbed, but an immediate television review ordered by referee Andrew Brace was inconclusive, with no evidence of the incident. However, since the incident was noted in the referee's report, it can be reviewed by the citing commissioner Peter Ferguson. "Leinster Rugby's Tadhg Furlong has been cited for an incident that occurred in the 37th minute of the United Rugby Championship Round 4 fixture at the Aviva Stadium against Munster Rugby on Saturday, 24 October," a statement from the URC said on Monday. "The Citing Commissioner in charge has made a complaint about an act of foul play by the Player (Tadhg Furlong No. 3) against opponent Gavin Coombes (No. 8). "The Player has been cited under Law 9.27 – A player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship, including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals. "Arrangements for the disciplinary process are currently in progress and will be announced in due course." Coombes has been backed in his allegation by Munster coach Clayton McMillan. "All I know is that I back our players 100% – that if they make an allegation like that, they wouldn't do it lightly – and that's not the sort of person Gavin is, so we'll see where that goes," McMillan said. Furlong faces the possibility of a lengthy ban if found guilty. The 33-year-old is a British & Irish Lion and key member of the Ireland team, approaching 100 test caps. He is in the squad for November's Nations Championship fixtures, and a ban would be a blow to his personal reputation as well as to the Irish team. Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said: "Obviously, once that accusation is made, it becomes a serious matter for the citing commissioner. So my comment is not going to help in any way here. But from what I've seen, I can't see anything." In the URC last season, Bulls hooker Jan-Hendrik Wessels was handed a nine-week suspension for grabbing the testicles of Connacht's Josh Murphy.

item.title: Ações fecham em alta, com pedido de IPO da Anthropic impulsionando papéis do setor de IA
item.description: As ações nos EUA fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira, com o S&P 500 e o Nasdaq saindo de quedas semanais consecutivas, já que o pedido de abertura de capital da Anthropic ajudou a impulsionar o otimismo em relação aos papéis ligados à IA, em uma semana repleta de diversos catalisadores de mercado.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: As ações nos EUA fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira, com o S&P 500 e o Nasdaq saindo de quedas semanais consecutivas, já que o pedido de abertura de capital da Anthropic ajudou a impulsionar o otimismo em relação aos papéis ligados à IA, em uma semana repleta de diversos catalisadores de mercado. A Anthropic divulgou perdas acentuadas e um crescimento vertiginoso da receita em seu pedido de oferta pública inicial nos EUA, expondo sua ambição de construir sistemas de IA capazes de remodelar a economia global, apesar dos altos custos de desenvolvimento da tecnologia. O laboratório de IA segue em frente com seus planos de abertura de capital, mesmo com a desaceleração do calendário de IPOs do outono — antes bastante movimentado —, já que a recente volatilidade do mercado levou as empresas a adiar suas ofertas. O pedido da Anthropic surge em um momento em que os investidores analisam cada vez mais o retorno potencial dos gastos maciços com IA e no início de uma semana agitada. Estão previstos a declaração de política monetária do Federal Reserve na quarta-feira, dados sobre crescimento econômico e inflação na quinta-feira e uma série de relatórios de resultados corporativos ao longo da semana. Mais de um terço das empresas do S&P 500 devem divulgar seus resultados financeiros esta semana, incluindo as gigantes da tecnologia Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) e Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , cujos resultados serão analisados em busca de sinais de que os vultosos investimentos em IA estejam se traduzindo em crescimento. “Hoje o foco está todo no pedido da Anthropic, então estamos de volta a uma postura um pouco mais otimista, eu diria. Mas há muita coisa nesse pedido. Será interessante ver como as coisas serão recebidas quando elas realmente forem listadas”, disse JP Powers, diretor de investimentos da RWA Wealth Partners, em Boston. “O risco é talvez um pouco de oscilação se as coisas não estiverem todas indo na mesma direção. Um pouco de otimismo hoje, mas quem sabe o que vai acontecer com alguns desses outros lançamentos nesta semana”, disse ele. O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 0,28%, para 52.361,58 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançou 0,70%, para 7.676,77 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) teve alta de 0,83%, para 26.169,38 pontos. Empresas do setor de chips e relacionadas a chips, amplamente consideradas como algumas das maiores beneficiárias do boom da IA, ajudaram a impulsionar os ganhos. O índice Philadelphia de chips (.SOX) subiu 2,8% no dia, mas ainda apresenta queda de 12,2% no mês. As ações da Meta fecharam em queda de 1,9% depois que a empresa de mídia social anunciou que planeja levantar até US$95 bilhões em capital para financiar sua expansão relacionada à IA em data centers, capacidade de computação em nuvem e outras infraestruturas. O setor de IA tem enfrentado pressões neste mês em meio a preocupações de que os gastos financiados por dívida possam se tornar mais difíceis de justificar diante do aumento dos custos de empréstimos. O pedido de registro da Anthropic ajudou a impulsionar o otimismo, no entanto, já que empresas de “neocloud”, incluindo a CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , recuperaram as perdas anteriores. Outras empresas ligadas à IA, incluindo as fabricantes de produtos fotônicos Lumentum (LITE.O) e Coherent (COHR.N) , estiveram entre as ações com melhor desempenho do S&P 500. A Lumentum e a Coherent subiram cerca de 8% e 6%, respectivamente. O índice de tecnologia (.SPLRCT) liderou os ganhos entre os 11 principais setores do S&P 500, subindo 1,5%. As ações de megacap e de crescimento também apresentaram, em sua maioria, alta. A Tesla (TSLA.O) subiu 5,2%, fechando em seu nível mais alto em mais de três meses, depois que o Barclays elevou sua recomendação para a ação de “neutro” para “acima da média do mercado”. Os mercados estão precificando apenas 12,7% de chance de um aumento nas taxas pelo Fed na quarta-feira, de acordo com o CME FedWatch. Mas, com as pressões inflacionárias não mostrando sinais de abrandamento, os participantes do mercado não acreditam que o banco central permanecerá com as taxas inalteradas por muito tempo. Os investidores também se preparam para as eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que decidirão o controle do Congresso dos EUA.

item.title: Petróleo fecha em queda com esperanças de paz; ataques à Arábia Saudita limitam perdas
item.description: Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam em queda nesta segunda-feira, em meio a esperanças de uma redução das hostilidades no Oriente Médio; no entanto, os ataques persistentes à Arábia Saudita — um dos principais produtores — e ao transporte marítimo mantiveram os investidores cautelosos, com os preços oscilando próximos às máximas dos últimos seis meses.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Cavale
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam em queda nesta segunda-feira, em meio a esperanças de uma redução das hostilidades no Oriente Médio; no entanto, os ataques persistentes à Arábia Saudita — um dos principais produtores — e ao transporte marítimo mantiveram os investidores cautelosos, com os preços oscilando próximos às máximas dos últimos seis meses. O Brent encerrou o dia com queda de 0,8%, a US$115,81 o barril, enquanto os contratos futuros do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos Estados Unidos fecharam com queda de US$1,51, ou 1,46%, a US$101,76 o barril. Ambos os índices de referência recuaram após fortes ganhos na sexta-feira, quando o Brent fechou com alta de mais de US$3, registrando um ganho semanal de 6%, enquanto o WTI subiu 2,3% na semana. O foco dos investidores permaneceu nas tensões no Oriente Médio depois que os houthis do Iêmen, alinhados ao Irã, afirmaram ter atacado estações de bombeamento no oleoduto leste-oeste da Arábia Saudita e no aeroporto de Riade no fim de semana. Não houve confirmação imediata da Arábia Saudita sobre os ataques houthis. A coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita no Iêmen, no entanto, informou nesta segunda-feira que havia destruído três drones que tinham como alvo Riade e as regiões do sul do reino. As esperanças de um avanço diplomático no conflito do Oriente Médio — que começou com ataques dos Estados Unidos e de Israel ao Irã e posteriormente se espalhou para a Arábia Saudita e o Iêmen — pesaram sobre os preços do petróleo no início do pregão, com o Brent caindo mais de US$2 por barril. Mediadores do Catar viajaram para Teerã no domingo, em coordenação com os Estados Unidos, para buscar maneiras de amenizar as tensões regionais, segundo uma autoridade a par do assunto. A Arábia Saudita, a Turquia e o Paquistão mantiveram conversações com autoridades iranianas em Teerã nesta segunda-feira, como parte dos esforços para evitar uma nova escalada na região. As negociações representaram o primeiro contato de alto nível entre o Irã e as três nações, que assinaram um pacto de defesa mútua em agosto. Ao final, os quatro países concordaram em continuar as negociações com o objetivo de fortalecer a cooperação em prol da paz e da segurança, informou a mídia estatal iraniana. O Parlamento egípcio autorizou o presidente Abdel Fattah al-Sisi a tomar “todas as medidas necessárias” para ajudar a Arábia Saudita a se defender, aumentando a possibilidade de apoio militar egípcio ao reino.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em queda de quase 14% após reeleição de Lula acionar "circuit breaker"
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou com a maior queda desde 2020 nesta segunda-feira, marcada por "circuit breaker" na bolsa paulista, em meio a uma forte reprecificação das ações brasileiras após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva conquistar a reeleição no domingo.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded:
O Ibovespa fechou com a maior queda desde 2020 nesta segunda-feira, marcada por "circuit breaker" na bolsa paulista, em meio a uma forte reprecificação das ações brasileiras após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva conquistar a reeleição no domingo. Investidores vinham se posicionado para uma vitória do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da disputa, principalmente após ele liderar a primeira etapa da disputa, vislumbrando um governo mais favorável ao mercado e melhora do cenário fiscal. Mas, no domingo, Lula [USN:L6N46C00S TEXT:"venceu"] Flávio por 51,79% a 48,21% dos votos válidos, uma diferença de 4,4 milhões de votos, frustrando tais expectativas e desencadeando uma forte correção no mercado financeiro brasileiro como um todo. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) despencou 13,88%, a 176.608,23 pontos, maior perda percentual em um dia desde 16 março de 2020 (-13,92%), período marcado pela pandemia de Covid. No pior momento do dia, o Ibovespa apurou queda de mais de 17%, a 169.516,43 pontos. O índice Small Caps (.SMLL) tombou 26,92%, para 2.036,13 pontos, maior queda em um dia da sua série histórica, iniciada em 2005. O volume financeiro no pregão totalizou quase R$114,9 bilhões, bem acima de uma média diária já alta no mês, de cerca de R$57,5 bilhões e perto do recorde registrado em abril desse ano, quando atingiu R$120 bilhões, inflado naquela sessão pelo vencimento de opções sobre o Ibovespa. FREIOS ACIONADOS A B3 acionou o "circuit breaker" na abertura, suspendendo por 30 minutos a negociação de ativos à vista, renda fixa privada e opções referenciadas em ações, BDR, Ibovespa, Ibovespa B3 BR+, IBrX-50, Índice Small Cap e ETFs. A B3 afirmou que decisão de acionar o mecanismo baseou-se na análise do cenário de formação do preço teórico do Ibovespa, que indicava queda superior a 20%. O "circuit breaker" não era acionado na bolsa desde março de 2020. "O mercado embutiu nos seus preços uma expectativa diferente no primeiro turno do que efetivamente se concretizou no segundo turno e como esse resultado foi diametralmente diferente das expectativas há esse ajuste forte", afirmou a investidora Louise Barsi, cofundadora do Grupo AGF (Ações Garantem o Futuro). "O momento é de cautela, mas não é nem 8 nem 80, não acho que é para zerar o caixa, mas também não acho que é para deixar algumas oportunidades passarem, principalmente nomes de qualidade", afirmou, lembrando que políticos passam, mas as boas empresas ficam e as oportunidades surgem justamente nesses momentos de grande instabilidade e incerteza. Olhando para frente, Louise citou que não dá para cravar que esse foi o único ajuste e citou que há um cenário desafiador para 2027, com baixo crescimento econômico, risco persistente de pressão inflacionária e juros ainda em níveis elevados. "Vamos ver se o governo vai fazer algum aceno ao mercado para tentar acalmar os ânimos", disse a investidora, que é filha de Luiz Barsi Filho, um dos maiores investidores individuais da bolsa brasileira. ACENO Ainda nesta segunda-feira, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou ao Estadão que o governo apresentará uma [USN:L2N46C0V8 TEXT:"proposta"] para que possa perseguir o centro da meta fiscal ao longo do ano, e não mais o piso da margem de tolerância. Na visão de agentes financeiros, houve um aumento das incertezas sobre as perspectivas fiscais do país e a direção dos preços dos ativos brasileiros agora dependerá das sinalizações sobre a política econômica do novo mandato. As atenções estão voltadas para a decisão sobre quem comandará o Ministério da Fazenda, bem como uma definição mais precisa da estratégia de consolidação fiscal para os próximos quatro anos. O Goldman Sachs espera, "no máximo, medidas modestas para conter o crescimento dos gastos primários, acompanhadas por novos aumentos de uma carga tributária que já é elevada. "O governo provavelmente manterá sua forte convicção de que o setor público e as estatais devem continuar desempenhando papel central como motores do crescimento econômico e do investimento", acrescentou em relatório a clientes. Para o Morgan Stanley, há, de modo geral, um risco relevante de queda para as ações brasileiras antes do fim do ano, especialmente para empresas mais expostas ao mercado doméstico. "Apesar de acreditar que a reação inicial dos mercados deve ser uma forte redução de exposição ao risco, o desafio subjacente é muito mais profundo, refletindo desequilíbrios macroeconômicos estruturais que se tornam cada vez mais difíceis de reverter." O Scotiabank também destacou que o fato de Flávio [USN:S0N461031 TEXT:"se recusar"] a reconhecer a derrota e entrar com uma contestação judicial do resultado deve manter a incerteza política elevada, mantendo sob pressão as ações brasileiras. "Continuamos otimistas em relação ao Brasil, mas pode ser necessário ter mais paciência", afirmou. DESTAQUES BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) desabou 29,33%, fechando em uma mínima desde maio de 2023, a R$17,47, em sessão [USN:S0N45001K TEXT:"bastante negativa"] para o setor financeiro, que vinha também sendo um dos mais beneficiados pelas expectativas de vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro. BTG PACTUAL UNIT tombou 24,83%, BRADESCO PN despencou 21,7%, ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN caiu 13,66% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT <SANB11.SA>, que divulga balanço na quarta-feira, fechou em queda de 4,47%.

B3 ON (B3SA3.SA) caiu 36,28%, enquanto XP <XP.O>, listada nos EUA, afundou 48,36%, na maior queda em um dia desde o IPO em 2019, e Nubank (NU.N) , também listada em Nova York, recuou 16,95%. Para analistas do JPMorgan, há risco de revisões negativas para as estimativas de mercado para o lucro por ação nos próximos dias e 2027 pode se mostrar um ano mais desafiador para o cenário macroeconômico brasileiro. O índice do setor financeiro (.IFNC) caiu 22,48%. PETROBRAS PN recuou 8,18% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) perdeu 6,81%, também contaminadas pela aversão a risco na bolsa brasileira, em pregão ainda marcado pelo declínio dos preços do petróleo no mercado internacional . A presidente da estatal, [USN:S0N43906C TEXT:"Magda Chambriard"], afirmou nesta segunda-feira que a forte queda nas ações se trata de "movimento especulativo" e não reflete os fundamentos da empresa. "A hora é de comprar (ações). Infelizmente não posso", disse a executiva à Reuters. VALE ON (VALE3.SA) subiu 4,01%, descolada do viés vendedor no pregão paulista, assim como outras exportadoras, em meio à forte valorização do dólar ante o real. No fechamento, a cotação acusou R$5,4066, alta de 8,36%. Na máxima do dia, chegou a superar os R$5,60. SUZANO ON (SUZB3.SA) avançou 10,08% e EMBRAER ON (EMBJ3.SA) fechou com elevação 8,89%, na ponta positiva do Ibovespa, assim como WEG ON (WEGE3.SA) , que valorizou-se 4,21%, em pregão ainda marcado pelo anúncio de compra do negócio de Power Controls Solutions (PCS) da empresa norte-americana L&S Electric por US$11 milhões. GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) fechou em alta de 0,91% antes da divulgação do balanço do terceiro trimestre, após o fechamento do mercado. A companhia tem parte relevante da receita oriunda da América do Norte. No setor, USIMINAS PNA perdeu 10,71% e CSN ON (CSNA3.SA) tombou 17,46%. MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) derreteu 58,23%, em dia de forte pressão em papéis sensíveis a juros dado o movimento na curva de DIs. O índice de consumo (.ICON) da B3 caiu 26,39%, enquanto o índice do setor imobiliário (.IMOB) perdeu 29,11%, com CYRELA ON (CYRE3.SA) despencando 44,81%.

item.title: Rubio dice que es necesario renovar infraestructura electoral de Venezuela antes de sufragios
item.description: El secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, dijo el lunes que la infraestructura electoral de Venezuela estaba diseñada para amañar las elecciones y que, por lo tanto, debía sustituirse rápidamente antes de que pueda haber una elección válida.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, dijo el lunes que la infraestructura electoral de Venezuela estaba diseñada para amañar las elecciones y que, por lo tanto, debía sustituirse rápidamente antes de que pueda haber una elección válida. Rubio habló con periodistas por teléfono un día después de que la líder de la oposición, María Corina Machado, regresó a Venezuela por primera vez desde que Estados Unidos capturó en enero al entonces presidente del país, Nicolás Maduro, y lo llevó a Nueva York para ser juzgado. Estados Unidos cree que las conversaciones entre el Gobierno interino de Caracas y los políticos de la oposición darán lugar a la creación de un nuevo Tribunal Supremo de Justicia a finales de este año y de un nuevo Consejo Electoral poco después, había dicho antes un alto funcionario del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos. "Creo que estamos logrando avances reales en ese sentido", dijo Rubio. "Pero si alguien intenta descarrilar el proceso, estará causando un gran daño a Venezuela". El Gobierno de Maduro estableció la infraestructura electoral del país para amañar las elecciones, por lo que debe cambiarse rápidamente, añadió Rubio.

item.title: Neil Young sues Trump again over 'Rockin' In The Free World'
item.description: Rock star Neil Young sued a group associated with President Donald Trump for copyright infringement in Virginia federal court on Monday over the president's alleged misuse of his song "Rockin' in the Free World" at an October rally.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Rock star Neil Young sued a group associated with President Donald Trump for copyright infringement in Virginia federal court on Monday over the president's alleged misuse of his song "Rockin' in the Free World" at an October rally. Young said in the complaint against the Trump 47 Committee that his 1989 song was played without a license before Trump took the stage at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, in support of Republican midterm election candidates on October 12 "The lyrics paint vivid street-level portraits -- a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity -- while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn't shared at all," the complaint said. "In short, the song is the opposite of everything Donald J. Trump stands for." Spokespeople for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint Young [USN:KCN250300 TEXT:"previously sued"] the Trump campaign in 2020 for using "Rockin' in the Free World" and another Young song at campaign rallies without permission According to the complaint, the campaign promised never to use "Rockin' in the Free World" again without a license after [USN:L1N2IN2SH TEXT:"settling"] the case later that year Young asked the Virginia court on Monday for $10 million in damages The case is Young v. Trump 47 Committee Inc, US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, No. 3:26-cv-01398 For Young: Robert Besser of the Law Offices of Robert Besser For the organization: attorney information not yet available Read more: [USN:KCN250300 TEXT:"Neil Young sues Donald Trump's campaign for using his songs"] [USN:L1N2IN2SH TEXT:"Neil Young ends lawsuit against Donald Trump's campaign over use of his songs"]

item.title: Shane Steichen keeping Daniel Jones as Colts' starting QB
item.description: Colts coach Shane Steichen once again told reporters Monday that Daniel Jones will remain Indianapolis' quarterback for the team's game at Jacksonville this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colts coach Shane Steichen once again told reporters Monday that Daniel Jones will remain Indianapolis' quarterback for the team's game at Jacksonville this week. Steichen said after the Colts' 16-10 loss to Minnesota on Sunday to fall to 2-5 that he had previously given no consideration to a change at QB. "He knows he's got to play better," Steichen told reporters Monday. "He's proven that he can do it. So that's where the confidence comes from. And we need to get him back playing to that level that he was last year. It's taking a little bit longer." Jones completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 13 games last season, his first with the Colts, before tearing his Achilles. This season, he's completing a career-low 59.6% of his passes for 1,398 yards with four touchdowns and seven interceptions -- one off the NFL lead. He has one TD and four interceptions in Indianapolis' last four games. Jones, 29, was the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft. He's thrown for 19,081 yards, 93 TDs and 62 picks over 90 career games for the Giants (2019-24) and Colts. Anthony Richardson Sr., Indianapolis' fourth overall pick in the 2023 draft, is the team's backup QB. He's appeared in 17 games (15 starts) and completed 50.6% of his passes for 2,400 yards, 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. --Field Level Media

item.title: US judge refuses to block Eli Lilly weight-loss drug ads, rules against Novo Nordisk
item.description: A US judge rejected on Monday Novo Nordisk's request to block Eli Lilly from continuing advertisements for weight-loss drugs that the Danish drugmaker considered false and misleading, affecting markets with tens of billions of dollars of annual sales.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: A US judge rejected on Monday Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) request to block Eli Lilly (LLY.N) from continuing advertisements for weight-loss drugs that the Danish drugmaker considered false and misleading, affecting markets with tens of billions of dollars of annual sales. US District Judge Zahid Quraishi in Trenton, New Jersey, said Novo Nordisk did not deserve a preliminary injunction, having failed to show that Eli Lilly's ads threatened sales, undermined its goodwill, or caused lasting damage to its clinical reputation. Quraishi called Novo Nordisk's claim of irreparable harm "inadequate to warrant the extraordinary relief it seeks." The judge ruled after a two-day hearing in late August. Novo Nordisk [USN:L1N43N0EQ TEXT:"sued"] Eli Lilly in July, saying ads for the obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro violated federal and state false advertising and unfair competition laws by comparing higher doses of those products with lower doses of Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Ozempic. One commercial included a voiceover claim, with a written disclaimer, that people using Zepbound on average lost 50 pounds (23 kg) while people using Wegovy on average lost 33 pounds (15 kg). "While we are disappointed with the court’s decision, today's ruling did not decide the question of whether Lilly's advertising is false and misleading, and this litigation is still ongoing," a Novo Nordisk spokesperson said in an email. "Everyone deserves clear, accurate and up-to-date information when making decisions about their health." Eli Lilly, based in Indianapolis, has denied wrongdoing and said it was pleased with the decision. WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS ARE BIG BUSINESS Weight-loss drugs have become major businesses for large pharmaceutical companies. The United States is among a handful of countries that allow direct-to-consumer advertising of prescription medicines. In his 25-page decision, Quraishi said that while Novo Nordisk's witnesses were credible, Eli Lilly's ads had at most a negligible market impact between April and July, with prescriptions for Novo Nordisk's products remaining stable. The judge said money damages could compensate Novo Nordisk for any "nontrivial harm" it might suffer absent an injunction. Quraishi also found Novo Nordisk's case "less than persuasive" based on a "very preliminary record," though he did not rule on the merits. Novo Nordisk reported combined sales of about $32 billion for obesity medicines and Ozempic in 2025, court papers show. The drugmaker is working to regain market share in the United States for its injectable obesity drugs, a market projected to exceed $100 billion by the end of the decade.

item.title: Rubio says Venezuela's electoral infrastructure must be replaced before a vote
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Venezuela's electoral infrastructure was designed to rig elections and so must be quickly replaced before a valid election can be held.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Venezuela's electoral infrastructure was designed to rig elections and so must be quickly replaced before a valid election can be held. Rubio spoke to reporters by phone a day after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela for the first time since the US captured the country's then-President Nicolas Maduro in January and took him to New York for trial. The US believes that talks currently underway between the interim government in Caracas and opposition politicians are expected to see a new supreme judicial tribunal in place by the end of this year and a new electoral council shortly thereafter, a senior US State Department official said earlier. "I think we're making real progress in that regard," said Rubio, who has acted as US President Donald Trump's point person on Venezuela. "But if anybody tries to derail that process, they're doing a great harm to Venezuela." Maduro's government had set up the country's electoral infrastructure to rig elections so must be quickly changed, Rubio added. But Rubio stopped short of giving a target date for elections. Machado has said elections should be held by mid-2027, though Trump has previously said he did not believe Venezuela was ready for a nationwide vote. Machado's return to Venezuela after several failed attempts risks straining her ties with Trump's administration. Nobel Peace Prize laureate Machado, who was prevented from challenging Maduro for the presidency in 2024, had been out of the country for 10 months and spent the previous year in hiding following the disputed election. Washington has said Machado has every right to be in Venezuela, but has praised acting President Delcy Rodriguez and supports a negotiation process between the Rodriguez government and opposition groups that do not include Machado's Vente Venezuela movement. Rubio said the only time he had "discouraged" Machado from going back to Venezuela was in the immediate aftermath of devastating earthquakes in the summer, because the country was grappling with a humanitarian crisis. But Rubio said that weeks ago the US told Venezuela's interim authorities that Machado "belongs in her country" and "should be allowed to return unperturbed," and the government had agreed. Asked about Machado's criticism of an oil deal that Trump had struck with the interim rulers, Rubio insisted that the agreement was a good one for both countries but that she had a right to express her opinion on the matter. Trump has repeatedly expressed support for Rodriguez, a former deputy to Maduro, and hailed deals on oil production and other business ventures by US companies in the South American country. But some critics have accused Trump of a neo-colonialist approach to Venezuela aimed at exploiting its natural resources. A faction of the opposition and the interim government held a round of talks this month, with the aim of remaking the top court and electoral council, among other goals, ahead of eventual elections. The talks have not included Machado's political movement.

item.title: Ben & Jerry's founders explore deal to separate brand from owner, WSJ reports
item.description: Ben & Jerry's founders Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield are exploring a deal to separate their brand from its current owner, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ben & Jerry's founders Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield are exploring a deal to separate their brand from its current owner, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. The ice cream brand is owned by Unilever (ULVR.L) spin-off Magnum Ice Cream (MICCT.AS) . The co-founders have been discussing a deal with Pete Stavros, founder of Expanding ESOPs, to carve out the business and structure it under an employee stock-ownership plan, WSJ said, citing Stavros and Cohen. The structure would give rank-and-file employees stock while providing the company with tax benefits, the report added. But any deal would need to be approved by Ben & Jerry's owner Magnum, which told Reuters in an emailed statement that "Ben & Jerry's is not for sale and, more importantly, is thriving as part of The Magnum Ice Cream Company." "Taking Ben & Jerry's out of Magnum would drive significant dis-synergies, investment in the social mission would fall, and selling prices per unit would inflate," it added. Ben & Jerry's has a history of vocal social activism and its founders and board have [USN:L6N40E1GS TEXT:"repeatedly clashed"] with former parent Unilever over political and ethical stances. Magnum has also looked to [USN:L1N41J0MN TEXT:"weaken the control"] of Ben & Jerry's independent board, which has been reduced to just two members. Cohen told the WSJ that "all he could do is try to generate more public pressure on Magnum to sell." Ben & Jerry's and representatives for the co-founders and Stravos did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

item.title: Trump afirma, sem provas, que eleição no Brasil parece ter sido manipulada
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, disse nesta segunda-feira que a eleição brasileira, vencida no domingo pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, parece ter sido fraudada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, disse nesta segunda-feira que a eleição brasileira, vencida no domingo pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, parece ter sido fraudada. "Não tomei partido, mas parecia mais uma eleição fraudulenta", disse ele a jornalistas, sem apresentar nenhuma evidência. "As eleições precisam ser incontestáveis, e isso me pareceu muito ruim." Derrotado no segundo turno da eleição, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) se recusa a reconhecer o resultado. Na noite de domingo, o candidato do PL criticou a prorrogação por duas horas do horário de votação do pleito, apesar de seu próprio partido também ter pedido a extensão. Seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, foi um aliado próximo de Trump enquanto esteve no cargo. O governo Trump vinha saudando uma onda de recentes vitórias eleitorais da direita em outros países da América Latina. Trump disse ainda nesta segunda-feira gostar de Lula e se dar bem com ele. O vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin, reeleito na chapa de Lula no domingo, rebateu a declaração do presidente norte-americano, classificando-a como "totalmente equivocada". "Primeiro, não se interfere na política de outro país. Essa é uma regra basilar. Segundo, não tem nenhum referencial pra dizer isso. Aliás, o Brasil é um exemplo pro mundo. De urna eletrônica, de segurança jurídica. Democracia é assim. Você ganha eleição, você perde a eleição, é o povo que decide", disse Alckmin à Rede Vanguarda. O vice aproveitou para falar que agora é hora de seguir com as negociações tarifárias com os EUA. “Nós, encerrada a eleição, vamos continuar a negociação com os Estados Unidos para ter um bom acordo", afirmou.

item.title: DoorDash in talks to buy Instacart in roughly $17 billion deal, source says
item.description: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery-delivery platform at about $17 billion, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wang, Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: DoorDash (DASH.O) is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart (CART.O) in a deal that could value the grocery-delivery platform at about $17 billion, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday. A deal may be finalized as soon as Wednesday, although there are no guarantees it will come together, the person said. Instacart's deal talks with Uber (UBER.N) are no longer active, the person added. Shares of Instacart, which had a market value of about $13 billion as of Friday's close, rose about 8% in regular trading, while DoorDash fell around 6%. The Wall Street Journal first reported the developments on Monday. The food delivery industry has been grappling with rising labor costs, tighter regulation of delivery workers and growing competition after the pandemic-driven boom in online ordering faded. The potential deal comes as delivery companies expand into grocery and retail to drive growth beyond restaurant delivery, with DoorDash [USN:L4N3RE0BH TEXT:"buying"] Deliveroo and Uber acquiring [USN:KBN2470AP TEXT:"Postmates"] and Delivery Hero . If successful, the acquisition of Instacart would give DoorDash access to the platform's established marketplace and retailer ties, which it could combine with its own vast delivery network and customer base. The grocery platform has been exploring a possible sale and has held [USN:L4N4691PA TEXT:"preliminary discussions"] with potential buyers including Uber and DoorDash, the Information reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Instacart declined to comment when contacted by Reuters, while Uber and DoorDash did not immediately respond. "Strategically, DoorDash looks like the more natural fit for Instacart, given the complementary strengths of its restaurant delivery network and Instacart's grocery expertise," said Nick Smith, co-founder of growth strategy consultancy Manifesto Growth Architects. "For Uber, the opportunity would be to deepen its position as an everyday convenience platform. But an acquisition only makes sense if it delivers incremental customer value and profitable growth — not simply greater scale." Separately, Instacart said in a regulatory filing on Monday it would wind down its Caper Cart smart shopping-cart business by the end of the second quarter of 2027, expecting pre-tax charges of $55 million to $80 million related to the move.

item.title: Trump offers $1 million for tipoffs that lead to voter fraud convictions
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Monday the US would give $1 million to anyone who reported voter fraud that leads to an arrest and conviction, a week before midterm elections that polls show could prove difficult for his Republican Party.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Monday the US would give $1 million to anyone who reported voter fraud that leads to an arrest and conviction, a week before midterm elections that polls show could prove difficult for his Republican Party. BACKGROUND AND QUOTE: The Trump administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, for example by pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including political experts as well as Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. "Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. Some election officials have told Reuters they are preparing for potential federal interference in midterm elections. Trump has made false claims related to elections in the past, including not acknowledging his defeat in the 2020 elections. His supporters [USN:L6N3OH01A TEXT:"eventually stormed the US Capitol"] on January 6, 2021, in an unsuccessful attempt to prevent congressional certification of those elections. Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the House of Representatives and Senate. However, ahead of the midterm vote in which control of Congress is at stake, Trump's approval has remained low due to voter concerns about the high cost of living and rising fuel prices from the US-Israeli war on Iran .

item.title: US, Canada working on deal to ease steel, auto tariffs, sources say
item.description: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, two US and four Canadian sources said, as the two governments try to repair relations that soured after trade talks broke down in August.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, two US and four Canadian sources said, as the two governments try to repair relations that soured after trade talks broke down in August. The talks focus on tariffs imposed under Section 232 of US trade law, including up to 50% tariff on Canadian steel and a 25% tariff on autos, with negotiators discussing potential relief from those duties. Just [USN:L6N46C17B TEXT:"32%"] of Americans approve of US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in next week's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. Tariffs on Canadian imports have become a [USN:L6N4580Y1 TEXT:"political liability"] for Trump, with Republican candidates in border states calling for an end to the trade war with Canada. One Canadian source briefed on the negotiations said a deal on steel and auto tariffs was possible before the November 3 elections, while US sources said the Trump administration wanted Canada to make further concessions. The sources spoke on condition of anonymity because the talks are private. The Section 232 tariffs are administered by the Commerce Department, putting Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick rather than the US Trade Representative's office at the center of the negotiations, sources on both sides of the border said. Lutnick and Canada's Dominic LeBlanc, the minister responsible for Canada-US trade, have been in regular contact recently, one of the sources said. "Canada remains in constructive dialogue with our U.S. counterparts on a range of priorities," a spokesperson for LeBlanc, said in a statement. "We stand ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada’s interests.” The US Trade Representative's Office and Canada have also been in contact in recent days regarding the overall architecture of any deal and all other trade issues, a USTR official said. The White House and the Commerce Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment. OTTAWA SEES PROGRESS Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there had been "a slight intensification" in talks with the United States, adding that Ottawa had not changed its stance. "To the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position," he told reporters, but did not give details. A Canadian industry source said a deal could come quickly, but not necessarily a broad one. "If it happens, it'll happen fast. But my sense is it'll be a narrowed deal, if it even happens,” the source said. Another Canadian source said they have believed for some time that a deal on Section 232 tariffs is likely before the midterms. Any agreement would be driven by Trump and Carney, the source said, adding that both leaders had said a mutually beneficial deal is possible. Carney has said he wants a [USN:O8N40E02J TEXT:"good deal "]for Canada. US and Canadian trade talks collapsed in August over issues such as whether to cut duties on medium- and heavy-duty vehicles that are critical for Canadian factories. US automakers [USN:L6N44N0VK TEXT:"had hoped"] the trade talks would deliver relief from Washington's original 25% tariffs that have raised the cost of shipping vehicles and parts across the border. Trump has previously announced that he would raise the tariffs on steel and auto imports from Canada to 50% from January 1, 2027. At a political rally on Sunday, Trump predicted the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics. Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit businesses in Maine.

item.title: STF não ordenou volta de Bolsonaro ao regime fechado após suposto desacato
item.description: O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) não determinou que o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, em prisão domiciliar desde novembro de 2025, retorne ao regime fechado, como afirmam posts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) não determinou que o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, em prisão domiciliar desde novembro de 2025, retorne ao regime fechado, como afirmam posts. “Urgente: Jair Bolsonaro é preso por desacato à autoridade e será enviado de volta para a Papuda”, dizem postagens que passaram a circular no Facebook e no Instagram neste domingo, após a vitória do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) sobre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O STF negou à Reuters que tenha havido uma decisão da Corte neste sentido. A determinação também não consta no processo de execução penal do ex-presidente, que cumpre pena de mais de 27 anos de prisão por tentar dar um golpe de Estado em 2022. A defesa do político disse por mensagem que “desconhece” uma ordem para que ele volte ao regime fechado e o alegado episódio de desacato. Até ser enviado para a prisão domiciliar , Bolsonaro foi mantido na prisão da Papudinha, que faz parte do Complexo Penitenciário da Papuda. A Polícia Militar do Distrito Federal, que administra a Papudinha, disse que a alegação sobre o retorno do ex-presidente "não procede". No fim da tarde desta segunda-feira, Flávio Bolsonaro publicou um vídeo em seu Instagram dizendo que havia visitado o pai em casa pela manhã. (Texto atualizado em 26 de outubro de 2026 com resposta da Polícia Militar do Distrito Federal e informação sobre visita de Flávio a Jair Bolsonaro.) VEREDICTO Falso. O STF, a defesa de Bolsonaro e a Polícia Militar do Distrito Federal negaram que o ex-presidente tenha sido enviado de volta ao regime fechado após um suposto episódio de desacato à autoridade. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . item.title: Alibaba AI model secretly tried to reach Beijing server in test, rival Cohere says
item.description: Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday one of Alibaba's Qwen AI models tried to send data to an Alibaba Cloud storage server in Beijing during a security test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday one of Alibaba's Qwen AI models tried to send data to an Alibaba Cloud storage server in Beijing during a security test. The model made the attempt even though its own reasoning indicated it would not do such a thing, Cohere said. Alibaba was not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Cohere, which sells its own AI models to businesses and governments as a "sovereign AI" provider, competes with open-weight models such as Alibaba's Qwen, which anyone can download and run on their own servers Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was asked to write a rule to detect malicious file download, but instead took stock of the machine it was running on and tried to send a test file to the Beijing server, Cohere said Cohere's test environment had no connection to the internet and blocked the attempt but the company said the request could have reached the server on a developer's laptop or a system with normal network access The behavior was rare, occurring in fewer than one in 100,000 actions across Cohere's tests, but a service handling 10 million agent actions a week could see as many as 100 such attempts, Cohere said The Canadian AI platform said it could not determine whether the behavior was deliberate or a leftover from the model's training, such as unscrubbed data from the environments where it was trained Chinese models accounted for 41% of downloads on AI platform Hugging Face over the past year, more than any other country's, according to the platform’s spring 2026 report

item.title: Libya says international aviation restrictions lifted after 11 years
item.description: Libya's Ministry of Transport said on Monday that airspace restrictions issued by the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization in 2015 during the country's civil war have been removed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Libya's Ministry of Transport said on Monday that airspace restrictions issued by the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization in 2015 during the country's civil war have been removed. The ministry said the decision, which was formally issued on October 23, was announced by ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar at the opening of a meeting of civil aviation officials from the Middle East in Doha. "This measure comes as a result of the notable progress made and the confidence placed in the capabilities of the Libyan civil aviation sector in recent times," the Tripoli-based Ministry of Transport said in a statement on its verified Facebook page. The ministry, in a separate statement, said the North African country has received requests for permits to transit Libyan airspace that it characterized as "unprecedented demand from international airlines." "The total number of permits registered for 2026-2027 winter season has surged to 61,968 flights per month, effective from this November," the ministry said, calling it a significant jump from an average of 2,000 transit flights per month during the 2025-2026 season. "Such an increase will generate substantial financial revenues using Libyan airspace," it added. Libya slid into chaos after the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011. Three years later, a civil war broke out between armed factions vying for power and divided the country between eastern and western administrations. The war caused damage to up to 20 aircraft, including Airbus (AIR.PA) models, at Tripoli International Airport in 2014. There are currently few airlines operating flights in and out of Libya, and they have long been limited to destinations such as Tunisia, Jordan, Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Sudan. The ICAO's decision would be circulated to all 193 member states for their implementation, the ministry added.
