item.title: CAE to sell airline operations software business Flightscape to SITA in $500 million deal
item.description: Canada's CAE on Monday said it will sell Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to fellow global aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's CAE (CAE.TO) on Monday said it will sell Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to fellow global aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Flightscape helps airlines plan flights, manage crews and coordinate ground and in-flight services The Flightscape deal comes five months after CAE first said it would pursue a [USN:L4N41O10J TEXT:"strategic review"] for that business CAE has stepped up efforts to lower costs and improve cash flow under CEO Matthew Bromberg, including an April job cut that impacted 280 workers The deal allows CAE to reshape its business around its core civil and defense operations CAE said it will put the proceeds from the Flightscape sale toward its core simulation and training businesses

item.title: Serbia's new leaders face host of tough challenges
item.description: Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in Sunday's parliamentary election, ending the long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named leaders face a long list of issues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Serbia's student-led protest movement [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"won a historic victory"] in Sunday's parliamentary election, ending the long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"leaders"] face a long list of issues. Here are a few of them: KOSOVO The Student List believes that Kosovo, which declared independence from Belgrade in 2008, remains an integral part of Serbia. During their campaign, the students' candidates said that Kosovo is a temporarily occupied territory which could be reintegrated into Serbia through peaceful means, diplomacy and dialogue. Their focus is preventing the exodus of the Serbian population in the north of Kosovo, and strengthening institutions funded by Serbia and operating under the Serbian legal system, such as healthcare and education. They want Kosovo's Serb communities to operate autonomously, rejecting previous agreements with the ethnic Albanian-led government in Pristina, such as those on energy, vehicle licence plates and the use of the dinar currency. FRAYED EU RELATIONS With Serbia's European Union accession talks largely stalled by a lack of necessary reforms, the Student List campaign deliberately avoided such polarising foreign policy issues. Prominent candidates, including former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, have said the government must first focus on domestic reforms and close all EU negotiating clusters before asking the public to cast a definitive ballot on membership of the bloc. The Student List position on Kosovo is also at odds with membership of the EU, which requires Belgrade to normalise relations with Pristina. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc [USN:L6N46B0AC TEXT:"stood ready to support reforms"] including on the rule of law and media freedom, and to work together to advance Serbia’s future in the EU. COMPLEX RUSSIAN RELATIONSHIP AND US SANCTIONS AGAINST NIS OIL FIRM The Student List must navigate an intricate energy and foreign policy web with traditional Serbian ally Russia. The students have said they have no plans to align with the EU and impose sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The new government would be reliant on US sanctions waivers to maintain crude imports while it waits for the [USN:L1N45M0TB TEXT:"sale of Russia's stake"] in energy company NIS (NIIS.BEL) , which operates Serbia's only oil refinery, to Hungary’s MOL (MOLB.BU) . Russia's Gazprom (GAZP.MM) is also Serbia’s biggest gas supplier, delivering around 2.2 billion cubic meters a year at below-market pricing. The Student List said this energy reliance was not a geopolitical alignment, but an acute economic dependency. The Student List's top candidates had not said whether a future government would end all arms exports from Serbia to war zones, including sales to Western intermediaries who pass weapons to Ukraine. Vucic cultivated strong personal ties with both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian President Vladimir Putin. CORRUPTION The Student List’s anti-corruption program centres on institutional overhauls, such as the creation of an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors rather than the Interior Ministry and a purge of police officers linked to organised crime or violent crackdowns on protests. They want a ban on the appointments of party loyalists to state-owned companies in favour of transparent, merit-based hiring. Financial accountability and fiscal oversight would include a strict asset origin law allowing the state to audit, seize and return illegally acquired wealth from officials to the state budget. Convicted officials would be barred from holding public office. The students' anti-corruption program also envisions public scrutiny of all major state infrastructure contracts and the creation of independent oversight bodies to curb the misuse of public funds. Vucic, the SNS and the authorities repeatedly denied accusations of repression and corruption. ECONOMY Serbia's economy is deeply integrated with both the European market and international investment flows. The IMF has forecast Serbia's economic growth at 3% in 2026 and 4% in 2027. Inflation in September stood at 4.1%, almost double August's 2.2%, while the central bank has maintained a 5.75% benchmark rate since 2024. The Student List’s economic platform shifts Serbia’s growth model away from state-backed infrastructure projects and cheap labour to domestic market security and labour rights. Central to the plan is a campaign against retail monopolies to lower food prices, coupled with a tax overhaul that raises levies on wealthy citizens and cuts them for lower-income groups. The movement has pledged to sharply lower the maximum allowed duration for temporary work. Fiscal sustainability would rely heavily on anti-corruption savings and rigorous state oversight. Social spending would be focused on curbing a youth exodus through an affordable housing initiative for young couples, teachers and healthcare staff, alongside guaranteeing free school textbooks and cheaper, state-subsidised medication.

item.title: La Jordanie dit avoir frappé des repaires de combattants en Syrie après l'attaque contre une église
item.description: La Jordanie a déclaré lundi que ses forces aériennes ont frappé des repaires de combattants dans le sud de la Syrie en réponse à l'attaque meurtrière de vendredi contre une église dans le sud du pays.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi, Yomna Ehab
item.content:encoded: La Jordanie a déclaré lundi que ses forces aériennes ont frappé des repaires de combattants dans le sud de la Syrie en réponse à l'attaque meurtrière de vendredi contre une [USN:L6N4690ZM TEXT:"église"] dans le sud du pays. Les forces de sécurité jordaniennes ont précisé que l'opération avait été menée en coordination avec Damas, ce que le régime syrien dément. Les autorités syriennes ont dit avoir ouvert une enquête sur les forces jordaniennes, soulignant l'importance de renforcer la coordination de la sécurité dans les régions frontalières. Damas a fait part de ses "réserves totales" au sujet de frappes qui ont été menées sans coordination préalable, a indiqué le ministère syrien des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Les frappes jordaniennes ont fait cinq morts civils, dont des femmes et des enfants, a annoncé un dirigeant sanitaire syrien à une agence de presse étatique. Amman n'a pas fourni de commentaire sur ces événements. Plus tôt, les forces de sécurité jordaniennes ont annoncé avoir arrêté trois suspects après l'attaque meurtrière perpétrée vendredi. Ces trois hommes, deux frères et leur beau-frère, ne semblent avoir aucun lien avec des cellules islamistes identifiées, ont déclaré de hauts responsables de la sécurité gouvernementale. "Si Dieu le veut, ils ne représentent qu'eux-mêmes", a déclaré le directeur de la sécurité publique jordanienne, le major-général Obeidallah al Maaytah, au cours d'une conférence de presse aux côtés du ministre de l'Intérieur Mazen al Faraya. "Le dossier n'est pas encore clos; les investigations se poursuivent. A ce jour, rien n'indique un lien entre eux et d'autres cellules", a précisé Mazen al Faraya. Le ministre de l'Intérieur a ajouté que les autorités examinaient les circonstances qui avaient poussé ces assaillants présumés vers l'extrémisme et qu'ils seraient tenus pour responsables si leur participation était confirmée. Les trois hommes sont soupçonnés d'avoir participé à une attaque survenue vendredi lors de funérailles dans une église grecque orthodoxe du village de Hamoud, dans le gouvernorat de Karak, situé à environ 120 km au sud-ouest d'Amman. Cette attaque a fait neuf morts et 40 blessés, suscitant la crainte au sein de la communauté chrétienne du pays. La Direction de la sécurité publique jordanienne a indiqué que les suspects avaient été localisés alors qu'ils se cachaient dans une maison abandonnée à Karak. Ils ont refusé de se rendre et ont attaqué les forces de sécurité, qui ont riposté et interpellé les trois hommes après les avoir blessés, a précisé la Direction dans un communiqué publié dans les médias d'État. Aucun membre des forces de sécurité n'a été blessé lors de l'interpellation, et plusieurs armes à feu ainsi que des munitions ont été retrouvées en possession des suspects. Le roi Abdallah II, dont le pays s'est allié aux Etats-Unis dans la lutte contre les groupes islamistes, a ordonné aux forces de sécurité de réagir avec une "main de fer" à cette attaque contre la minorité chrétienne.

item.title: "Retour vers le futur" au Brésil? Flavio Bolsonaro, comme jadis son père, refuse de reconnaître la victoire de Lula
item.description: Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a remporté dimanche un quatrième mandat historique.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a [USN:L5N46C021 TEXT:"remporté"] dimanche un quatrième mandat historique. Le sénateur de 45 ans conteste une décision prise dimanche soir par un juge de la Cour suprême nommé par Lula, qui a prolongé le second tour de l'élection présidentielle de deux heures en raison d’irrégularités présumées concernant le transport des électeurs. Le fils de Jair Bolsonaro a déclaré qu’il demanderait l’annulation du résultat. "Il est impossible de reconnaître les résultats de l’élection, compte tenu des circonstances dans lesquelles les événements se sont déroulés", a-t-il déclaré à des journalistes. Le président américain Donald Trump, autrefois proche allié du père Bolsonaro, a également fait part de ses doutes sur la validité du scrutin, faisant état d'une élection truquée". "Je n'ai pas pris parti, mais ça ressemble à une nouvelle élection truquée", a-t-il déclaré, sans fournir de preuves. Parallèlement, de nombreux dirigeants ont salué la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, les félicitations affluant de l'Union européenne, du Mexique, de la France, du Canada, de l'Inde et de la Russie. Les présidents de droite récemment élus en Colombie, au Pérou et au Chili ont également rejoint les rangs des dirigeants reconnaissant les résultats de dimanche, mais l'administration américaine du président Donald Trump, proche de la famille Bolsonaro, est restée silencieuse. Les investisseurs, stupéfaits par la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a déjoué les sondages, ont fait [USN:L6N46C0UL TEXT:"plonger la Bourse brésilienne"], le taux de change et la dette publique, alors que les marchés réévaluaient les perspectives budgétaires du pays. Toutefois, l’ampleur de la défaite, Bolsonaro fils accusant un retard de plus de 4 millions de voix sur Lula, rend peu probable le succès de sa tentative pour faire annuler le scrutin, selon des analystes. Sa requête est également compromise par le fait que son équipe avait elle-même demandé une prolongation des opérations de vote en raison de fortes pluies dans le sud du pays, traditionnellement conservateur. Moins de 35.000 suffrages, soit environ 0,03% du total, ont été exprimés au cours des deux heures supplémentaires de vote ordonnées par la Cour suprême, selon une analyse des registres électoraux réalisée par Pedro Burgos, professeur à l'Insper. Le refus du fils l'ancien président de reconnaître sa défaite pourrait néanmoins déclencher une vague de manifestations dans un pays où la confiance dans le système électoral et dans l’indépendance judiciaire a été mise à rude épreuve ces dernières années, estiment les observateurs. Jair Bolsonaro avait plongé le Brésil dans une profonde crise démocratique après les élections de 2022, lorsque ses partisans avaient pris d’assaut des bâtiments gouvernementaux pour protester contre le résultat. Il a par la suite été [USN:L5N3UY1NR TEXT:"condamné"] à 27 ans de prison. Il est depuis lors détenu à domicile, pour des raisons liées à son état de santé. INTERDICTION DE QUITTER LE BRÉSIL A la suite d'une visite à son père en prison, Flavio Bolsonaro a déclaré que la police fédérale brésilienne lui avait demandé de remettre ses passeports, ajoutant qu'il avait l'intention de coopérer avec les autorités, niant vouloir fuir le pays. Flavio Bolsonaro a accusé le juge de la Cour suprême Alexandre de Moraes d'être à l'origine de cette décision, sans apporter de preuves. La Cour suprême brésilienne et la police fédérale n'ont pas répondu à une demande de commentaire. "On m'a ordonné, en pleine rue, de remettre mes passeports, et on m'a notifié que j'avais pour interdiction de quitter le pays", a déclaré Flavio Bolsonaro dans une vidéo publiée sur ses réseaux sociaux. Ce dernier affirme que la décision du juge brésilien fait suite aux commentaires de son frère, Eduardo Bolsonaro, qui avait conseillé au candidat à la présidentielle la semaine dernière dans un podcast de fuir le Brésil s'il venait à perdre contre Lula. La victoire de Lula a déjoué les sondages, coupant court à une vague conservatrice en Amérique latine. Un résultat surprise qui n'est pas non plus du goût de l’administration du président américain Donald Trump, qui a oeuvré pour le retour du clan Bolsonaro au pouvoir. Les marchés financiers ont également exprimé leurs inquiétudes. Un fonds négocié en Bourse coté à Tokyo et indexé sur l’indice brésilien Bovespa (1325.T) a plongé de près de 15% lors des échanges asiatiques à l’annonce de la victoire de Lula, tandis que les analystes s’attendaient à ce que le real brésilien s’affaiblisse face au dollar américain. Lula s'était retrouvé en seconde position face à Flavio Bolsonaro au premier tour, mais il a réussi à mobiliser sa base dans l'entre-deux-tours. S’exprimant dimanche soir dans un hôtel de São Paulo, il a adopté un ton conciliant. "Je ne parlerai pas d’unité nationale, car cela ne correspond pas toujours à la réalité de ce pays. Personne n’est obligé d’apprécier le président élu, mais celui-ci a été mis en place pour gouverner au nom de tous", a-t-il souligné. Pendant la campagne, Lula, qui a 80 ans, a mis en avant son bilan en matière de lutte contre la pauvreté et les inégalités, tout en soulignant les taux historiquement bas du chômage, de l’analphabétisme et de la déforestation. Son quatrième mandat [USN:L6N46C0YC TEXT:"s'annonce difficile"]. Il devra en effet travailler au côté d’un Congrès tenu par les alliés de Bolsonaro, après une vague conservatrice aux élections législatives. Le président français Emmanuel Macron a déclaré que la France et le Brésil avaient "beaucoup à construire ensemble", tandis que la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a affirmé que "la démocratie et le multilatéralisme avaient triomphé au Brésil". Le Kremlin a salué la réélection de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et l’a félicité pour sa contribution aux relations bilatérales et au groupe des BRICS. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a félicité le dirigeant de gauche pour ses "résultats électoraux remarquables" et a déclaré qu’il se réjouissait à l’idée d’approfondir la coopération.

item.title: Trend hedge funds saw worst week since 2024 as AI stocks fell, Goldman says
item.description: Trend-following hedge funds witnessed their worst weekly performance in two years last week, as concern about the eventual pay-off from hefty AI spending ignited volatility across stocks and bonds, a Goldman Sachs note seen by Reuters on Monday showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Trend-following hedge funds witnessed their worst weekly performance in two years last week, as concern about the eventual pay-off from hefty AI spending ignited volatility across stocks and bonds, a Goldman Sachs note seen by Reuters on Monday showed. The Nasdaq 100 (.NDX) , home to the world's largest tech stocks, fell 5.5% last week, its biggest weekly fall since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs roiled world markets. Last week's stock market fall was led in part by a 10% weekly slide in shares of Meta (META.O) , which reported strong earnings, but indicated it would need to raise more capital for its AI investments, which sent shivers through markets. Bond markets were also volatile, as investors sought out the relative safety of US Treasuries, while selling the debt of more fragile economies, such as France. Here's what the note said: Systematic long-short hedge funds, whose algorithms ride market trends until they peter out, suffered their worst week since 2024, with a 2% decline, while fundamental long/short strategies drew down another 1.1%. Fundamental long short strategies are down 3.8% for the month so far, but still up 8.8% this year, while systematic strategies are down 1.1% so far in October, but up 18.7% so far this year. Single stocks collectively saw the largest de-gross activity - a general pulling back in positions - since late July, while US equities have been net sold for the third straight week, and in four out of the last five weeks, the note said Goldman said its prime brokerage desk reported $20 billion in selling of tech stocks over the last two weeks, close to July's major unwind in which saw $23 billion in selling.

item.title: French students vow more protests despite Macron government's concessions
item.description: French student leaders vowed to go on protesting despite government concessions on education, keeping pressure on President Emmanuel Macron as the movement spreads to unions and other activists, stokes unrest and deepens the economic damage.
item.dc:creator: Makini Brice, Inti Landauro
item.content:encoded: French student leaders vowed to go on protesting despite government concessions on education, keeping pressure on President Emmanuel Macron as the movement spreads to unions and other activists, stokes unrest and deepens the economic damage. The measures included a commitment to cap the size of some high school classes; €4 billion ($4.5 billion) of loans for renovating schools; and the replacement by 2028 of a university admissions system students see as socially unfair. "Not all our demands were met. We'll go on for as long as it takes," Louis Letoublon, one of the representatives of high school students, said as he and fellow student leaders emerged from a meeting with government officials in Paris. The protests, which have broadened beyond education to draw in trade unions and yellow-vest activists, known for their high-visibility jackets, pose a test for Macron's minority government. The government has little room to spend its way out of the unrest, with national debt approaching 120% of GDP, while the turmoil is boosting support for far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen ahead of next year's presidential election. The package included €1 billion of investment in university campuses; a move to increase student grants with inflation; and the opening up of a further 15,000 higher education places for students. "It's clear we have to ease the pressure being felt in the education system," Education Minister Edouard Geffray told a press conference. There was no overall figure for how much funding the package would require. High borrowing needs are already complicating efforts to [USN:L8N4660JK TEXT:"agree"] a budget for next year. The protests, initially triggered by student discontent, have shown little sign of ending [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"after violence"] nine days ago engulfed dozens of cities, leading to fears the state had lost control of the streets. Earlier, Macron acknowledged it was likely there would be more unrest this weekend ahead of a bigger nationwide day of protests set for November 5. On a tour to survey the damage in Marseille and to thank emergency services after Saturday's protests, he said he would keep security measures in place and work to move protests outside city centres. [USN:L5N46B05E TEXT:"Candidate"] Le Pen, already the frontrunner in next year's presidential election, has benefited from the unrest and perceptions that authorities are struggling to keep the peace. An opinion poll published on Sunday put her on 32% to 33.5%, well ahead of her nearest rival, hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon on 17%. Surveys suggest she would easily defeat Melenchon in a run-off ballot, expected to be held in early May. FAR-RIGHT GANGS CONFRONT FAR-LEFT ACTIVISTS Interior Minister Laurent Nunez earlier said that 1,435 people were arrested nationwide during demonstrations on Saturday and that police had also recorded a new phenomenon, with organised far-right gangs confronting far-left activists in several cities. "We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out, officially, to defend businesses," he said. "In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organised formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement." A selloff in French government bonds paused on Monday after rating agency [USN:L1N469154 TEXT:"Moody's"] on Friday refrained from downgrading the country's sovereign debt. But business leaders said the unrest was continuing to inflict heavy economic damage. Alain Di Crescenzo, head of the CCI France network of chambers of commerce and industry, said many retailers had remained closed as a precaution after the violence of October 17, adding this had led to sharp falls in sales. "We have shopkeepers who are tired and demoralised, and we are killing local commerce," he told Radio Classique.

item.title: Barril cae ante esperanzas de paz, ataques a Arabia Saudita limitan las pérdidas
item.description: Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Cavale
item.content:encoded: Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses. * Los futuros del crudo Brent bajaron 91 centavos, o un 0,8%, a 115,81 dólares, mientras que los futuros del West Texas Intermediate (WTI) cayeron 1,51 dólares, o un 1,46%, a 101,76 dólares por barril. * Ambos referenciales retrocedieron tras las fuertes ganancias registradas el viernes, cuando el Brent cerró con un alza de más de 3 dólares para acumular un incremento semanal del 6%, mientras que el WTI avanzó un 2,3% en la semana. * La atención de los inversores siguió centrada en la escalada de tensiones en Oriente Medio, después de que los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, dijeron haber atacado estaciones de bombeo del oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudita, así como el aeropuerto de Riad, durante el fin de semana. * Arabia Saudita informó el domingo que había interceptado más misiles y drones; por su parte, la coalición liderada por los saudíes comunicó el lunes la destrucción de tres drones que tenían como objetivo Riad y las regiones meridionales del reino. * En una medida que podría involucrar a Egipto de manera más directa en el conflicto, el Parlamento autorizó al presidente Abdel Fattah al-Sisi a adoptar "todas las medidas necesarias" para ayudar a Arabia Saudita a defenderse. Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán mantuvieron conversaciones con funcionarios iraníes en Teherán, como parte de los esfuerzos para evitar una mayor escalada en la región. EL encuentro supuso el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y las tres naciones, que firmaron un pacto de defensa mutua en agosto. Al término, los cuatro países acordaron continuar las conversaciones con el objetivo de reforzar la cooperación en materia de paz y seguridad, informaron los medios estatales iraníes.

item.title: Euro cae antes de reuniones de bancos centrales; el real brasileño se hunde
item.description: El euro cayó frente al dólar el lunes, ante una semana repleta de reuniones de los bancos centrales y con los precios del crudo aún en niveles elevados, mientras que el real brasileño se desplomó tras la sorprendente victoria electoral del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: El euro cayó frente al dólar el lunes, ante una semana repleta de reuniones de los bancos centrales y con los precios del crudo aún en niveles elevados, mientras que el real brasileño se desplomó tras la sorprendente victoria electoral del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. * El euro se vio presionado la semana pasada, ya que una ola de ventas de bonos del Estado francés llevó la prima de riesgo de la deuda del país a su nivel más alto desde la crisis de la deuda soberana de 2011, lo que reavivó las preocupaciones sobre una nueva crisis financiera en toda la zona euro. * Sin embargo, los precios de los bonos del Estado francés (OAT) subieron el lunes después de que Moody’s evitó la semana pasada una rebaja de la calificación crediticia de Francia, lo que alivió la presión sobre un Gobierno que lucha por reforzar sus finanzas. * El euro bajó un 0,21% frente a la moneda estadounidense, a 1,1179 dólares , pero subió un 0,31% ante su par japonés, a 176,04 yenes . * Los futuros del crudo Brent retrocedieron, pero se mantuvieron cerca de máximos de seis meses. Los elevados precios del petróleo lastran a las economías dependientes de las importaciones, como la zona euro. El Brent cayeron un 0,78%, a 115,81 dólares por barril. * El dólar se ha visto respaldado por unos indicadores económicos estadounidenses resistentes, a pesar de los obstáculos, entre ellos el aumento de la inflación. La moneda estadounidense se vio sometida a presiones vendedoras durante la corrección del mercado impulsada por el sector tecnológico la semana pasada. * Cinco bancos centrales importantes anunciarán sus decisiones de política monetaria a lo largo de esta semana. Se espera que la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos, el Banco Central Europeo y el Banco de Japón mantengan las tasas de interés sin cambios a pesar de las presiones inflacionarias. * El yen japonés cayó un 0,43%, a 157,46 unidades por dólar. * El índice dólar , que mide el comportamiento de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas, subió un 0,43%, a 102 unidades. * Mientras, el real brasileño se desplomó frente al dólar después de que Lula logró el domingo un histórico cuarto mandato frente al senador Flávio Bolsonaro, hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro. * El real cedió un 8,36%, a 5,4066 unidades por dólar, después de perder hasta un 12% más temprano.

item.title: TSX rises as investors welcome British Columbia election result
item.description: Canada's main stock index rebounded on Monday, led by financial and resource shares, after the result of British Columbia's provincial election potentially raised prospects for oil and gas companies.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rebounded on Monday, led by financial and resource shares, after the result of British Columbia's provincial election potentially raised prospects for oil and gas companies. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 155.98 points, or 0.4%, at 35,944.16, after posting on Friday its lowest closing level since October 14. The opposition Conservative Party won an [USN:L6N46B033 TEXT:"election"] in the province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production. "People are talking about the BC elections," said Barry Schwartz, chief investment officer at Baskin Wealth Management. "For oil and gas and construction companies, it's directionally positive." The energy sector (.SPTTEN) , which includes a number of companies with a market capitalization greater than C$100 billion ($71.34 billion), such as Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ.TO) and Suncor Energy (SU.TO) , rose 0.4%. [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled 1.5% lower but remained elevated at $101.76 a barrel. "The longer oil stays at these levels, you kind of have to own a CNQ or Suncor," Schwartz said. The materials group (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, was up 0.7%. item.title: Ambani, Adani outlets among Indian publishers contesting Modi’s privacy law
item.description: A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government last year announced implementation of a privacy law to [USN:L4N3WQ0V8 TEXT:"protect digital personal data"] of users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom. Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, India's Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters. The October 6 lawsuit, being reported for the first time and due to be heard on Tuesday, is the most high-profile challenge to Modi’s privacy law. Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller news outlets had [USN:L4N3ZZ10J TEXT:"challenged"] it. It also marks an unusual challenge to the government from businesses headed by Ambani and Adani, who opposition parties allege are close to Modi and get favourable treatment - charges the businesses and the government vehemently deny. DNPA and the media groups did not respond to requests for comment from Reuters, and neither did India's information technology ministry. The publishers are demanding that most of the law's contentious provisions, which kick in from May 2027, should be quashed. They are arguing the law could force a journalist to get prior consent from a person they want to investigate and force publishers to erase stories. They also say powers granted by the law to demand information could expose reporters' sources. The law would "render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder of events," the 698-page filing said. The provisions "constitute pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name". The lawsuit comes amid accusations of declining press freedom in India since Modi took office in 2014. Critics say many mainstream media outlets have [USN:L4N43Q0BR TEXT:"not done enough"] to scrutinise Modi’s government. India's ranking in Reporters Without Borders’ World Press Freedom Index fell to 157th out of 180 countries this year, from 140th in 2014 - but the government rejects the rankings. Modi's government says it respects press freedom and says India, which has a "vibrant press and media ecosystem" of hundreds of newspapers and TV channels, does not need validation from foreign bodies. CONCERNS OVER CONSENT DNPA's members include Ambani's Network18, which has seven digital news platforms, Adani's NDTV (NDTV.NS) and other marquee media groups including the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group, publisher of India's largest-selling English-language daily. A key concern in the law is the requirement of consent, the group's filing says. A social media platform or online retailer can seek consent from users when they sign up, but the DNPA has argued that requiring a journalist to notify the subject of an investigation and seek consent "would allow that subject to destroy evidence, intimidate witnesses". The law also lets people withdraw consent at any time and demand that their data be erased, without any public-interest safeguard, which DNPA says could force its members to unpublish or heavily redact a factual news report. FEAR OF SOURCES AT RISK News publishers are concerned that a federal authority created under the law can impose fines for non-compliance, and grants powers to New Delhi to block access to any information in the "interests of the general public", which would curtail press freedom, DNPA said. In an August letter to the government attached to the lawsuit, the group said India "has chosen to grant broad exemptions to the state, while failing to extend any corresponding protection to the press". No response was cited. From next year, the law will also let New Delhi order any organization handling personal data “to furnish such information as it may call for”, putting newsrooms at risk of having to divulge sources, the filing said. It can also deter whistleblowers from sharing information on corruption, corporate wrongdoing or electoral malpractice with reporters, the DNPA argued. The “nakedly unguided” provision must be quashed, the DNPA said, adding that the power “can extend to privileged communications in possession of a reporter or the informant.”

item.title: After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to learn how student-backed leaders will govern
item.description: Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a historic landslide election.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"historic landslide election"] that sparked nationwide celebrations, although few had an idea of how they would govern. Tens of thousands [USN:L6N46B0A6 TEXT:"took to the streets"] of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down. With almost 99% of votes counted, the students' candidates had secured a commanding 52.7% of the vote, according to the State Election Commission, versus 39.2% for Vucic's Serbia Progressive Party (SNS)-led alliance. That gives the students 139 seats in the 250-seat parliament, leaving the SNS alliance with 97, and the remainder held by minority parties. The constitution allows up to 90 days for the creation of a government, once the parliament is convened after the announcement of final results by the state election commission. "I thought it was unbelievable, I still do not believe it. It was too long, and (Vucic) was pressuring us for a long, long time," said university administrator Marijana Radovanovic Pajovic. Vucic dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president from 2014. But he was swept from power by a list of student-backed candidates [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"born out of anti-corruption protests"] following the deaths of 16 people in the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad. PROFOUND POLITICAL SHIFT The students' win marks a [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"profound political shift"] in the country of some 6 million people and is reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It may also offer inspiration to other [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"student movements"] that have [USN:L5N46B060 TEXT:"cropped up"] across Europe in recent weeks demanding better education standards and prospects. While the students' candidates include university professors, actors and farmers, the movement is without a leader - a strategy employed during protests to avoid any smear attempts by the government. It is unclear who will become prime minister and assume other key positions in order to enact the students' domestic agenda, which aims to root out graft and improve schooling, and manage the [USN:L6N46C0IX TEXT:"country's place on the international stage"]. "This corruption that has entered into all pores of our lives...of course it will change, we are hoping we will slowly go into that direction of a normal community," said 60-year-old insurance worker Svetlana Karagkozidou. Prominent figures include the head of the students' candidate list, cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, who spoke on behalf of the students following their victory. However, not everyone welcomed the change. "Changing the country like that so suddenly and all at once, I don’t like it. I don’t even know who is standing behind, who those people are, who will be leading the country," said 60-year-old civil worker Senka Radakovic. Meanwhile, supporters of the student movement set about cleaning up a park near the parliament building in Belgrade that had long been used as a camp by Vucic's supporters. They removed metal barricades and tents and cleaned stickers off children's play equipment. "I think it is one of Belgrade's most beautiful parks, that they took from us for a year or a year-and-a-half, and this is the least we can do right now," said one of the cleaning volunteers Filip Beselinovic. Vucic and the SNS repeatedly denied [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"accusations of repression and corruption"].

item.title: Equities end higher as Anthropic's IPO filing buoys AI stocks
item.description: US stocks closed higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming off consecutive weekly declines, as Anthropic's IPO filing helped boost sentiment in AI-related stocks in a week filled with a host of market catalysts.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: US stocks closed higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming off consecutive weekly declines, as Anthropic's IPO filing helped boost sentiment in AI-related stocks in a week filled with a host of market catalysts. [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"Anthropic disclosed"] steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, laying out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The AI lab is pushing ahead with its listing plans even as a once-lively autumn IPO calendar has slowed, with recent market volatility prompting companies to delay offerings. Anthropic's filing comes as investors increasingly dissect the potential payoff from massive AI spending and at the start of an eventful week. On tap are the Federal Reserve's policy statement on Wednesday, readings on economic growth and inflation on Thursday and a slew of corporate earnings reports throughout the week. More than a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , whose results will be [USN:L6N45T17Q TEXT:"parsed for signs"] of whether the hefty AI investments are translating into growth. "Today's all about the Anthropic release, so we're back on a little bit of an optimistic tilt, I would say. But there's a lot in that release. It will be interesting to see how well things are received when they actually come to list," said JP Powers, chief investment officer at RWA Wealth Partners in Boston. "The risk is maybe a little bit of a whipsaw if things aren't all moving in the same direction. A little optimism today, but who knows what will happen from some of these other releases this week," he said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 146.42 points, or 0.28%, to 52,361.58, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 53.09 points, or 0.70%, to 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 214.04 points, or 0.83%, to 26,169.38. Semiconductor and chip-related companies, widely viewed as some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, helped fuel the gains. The broader Philadelphia chips index (.SOX) was up 2.8% on the day but is still down 12.2% on the month. Meta shares closed down 1.9% after the social media company said it [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"plans to raise"] up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of climbing borrowing costs. The Anthropic filing helped buoy sentiment, however, as neocloud firms, including CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , erased earlier declines. Other AI-linked companies, including photonic product makers Lumentum (LITE.O) and Coherent (COHR.N) , were among the best-performing S&P 500 stocks. Lumentum and Coherent gained about 8% and 6%, respectively. The technology index (.SPLRCT) led gains among the 11 major S&P 500 sectors, climbing 1.5%. Megacap and growth stocks were also mostly higher. Tesla (TSLA.O) jumped 5.2% to close at its highest level in more than three months after Barclays upgraded its rating on the stock to "overweight" from "equal-weight." Markets are pricing in only a 12.7% chance of a rate hike from the Fed on Wednesday, according to CME FedWatch. But with inflation pressures showing no signs of abating, market [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"participants do not believe"] the central bank will be on hold for long. Investors are also bracing for the November 3 midterm elections , which will decide control of the US Congress. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.36-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and by a 1.09-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted seven new 52-week highs and seven new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 82 new highs and 349 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was 16.7 billion shares, compared with the 17.2 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.
